concept_purpose: Argues language is the carrier of culture and colonial language imposition colonizes consciousness, so reclaiming Indigenous languages is essential to decolonization
paper_title: African films and languages (Editorial)
paper_argument: Frames the African-language-films issue through Ngũgĩ, arguing African-language films are vital tools of self-representation and cultural export that embody cultural knowledge, identity and history and contribute to the African Renaissance and decolonization

concept_purpose: Language as the embodiment of culture; translation/subtitling choices either decolonize or recolonize the Indigenous-language film for non-native audiences
paper_title: Issues of subtitling in Biyi Bandele's Elesin Oba
paper_authors: Israel Ayinla Fadipe and Imoh Sunday Obot
paper_argument: Analyses subtitling lapses in Elesin Oba (2022, adapted from Soyinka's Death and the King's Horseman) through Ngũgĩ's Decolonising the African Mind, arguing translation for non-native audiences risks distorting the film's culturally embedded meaning

concept_purpose: A militant, anti-imperialist cinema of marginalized peoples that resists cultural relegation and Western mainstream aesthetics
paper_title: Preserving Indigenous Ovaherero cultural heritage in the digital age: Analysis of the film Tjipangandjara
paper_argument: Places the Namibian short Tjipangandjara in the Third Cinema tradition as resistance to cultural relegation and argues new filmless digital technology can promote Indigenous Ovaherero language and heritage, contra claims that modernization causes their extinction

concept_purpose: Explains how postcolonial sovereign power in Africa operates through commandment, spectacle and the management of who may live and who is left to die
paper_title: Jean-Pierre Bekolo's Le président: Documenting the absence
paper_argument: Reads Bekolo's banned mockumentary Le président through Mbembe's postcolony and necropolitics, arguing the film mocks documentary's visible evidence to expose presidents-for-life autocracy and provoke political dissent

concept_purpose: A speculative aesthetic projecting African/Black futures to critique present subjugation and counter Afro-pessimist framings of the continent
paper_title: Science fiction and masquerade in Jean-Pierre Bekolo's Les Saignantes (2005): A cinematic way out of Africa's declining future
paper_argument: Argues Les Saignantes deploys Afrofuturist aesthetics and a Mevungu-ritual female-gaze masquerade to critique Africa's postcolonial commandment power and the ethnologizing phallocentric gaze, using a dying future-universe as a warning mirror

concept_purpose: Names the colonial discourse that invented Africa as an object of Western knowledge, showing knowledge production is inseparable from colonial power
paper_title: The colonial library and productive futurity in Jean-Pierre Bekolo's Mudimbe's Things and Words (2015)
paper_argument: Argues Bekolo and Mudimbe deconstruct Foucault to show how the colonial library weaponizes the imposed colonial past as a precondition of ongoing power and violence in Africa

concept_purpose: An anticolonial cultural-political movement affirming Black identity and African cultural value as resistance to colonial denigration
paper_title: Death and negritude: Bekolo's Miraculous Weapons
paper_argument: Reads Bekolo's Miraculous Weapons (citing Césaire's Les Armes miraculeuses) as a meditation on art, life and death in which négritude becomes the movement that refuses to die under postcolonial tension

concept_purpose: Interrogates Africa not as a fixed entity but as a constructed idea whose meaning is continually produced, here through cinema as knowledge-practice
paper_title: Artistic epistemologies: Black cinema and the idea of Africa
paper_argument: Frames the special issue around what knowledge of contemporary Africa is deducible through its cinemas, citing Mbembe to link the idea of Africa with cultural ontologies and new possibilities for theorizing Africa cinematically

concept_purpose: Explains how a global film culture is constructed hegemonically by Western institutions that structurally omit African cinemas from history, criticism and industry
paper_title: Global silences on African cinemas: Dialectic of omission in western canons
paper_argument: Argues African cinemas are systematically omitted across the three fronts of Western-led global film canons and that even as world cinemas advance, African cinemas have not impacted global canon directions, reproducing a hegemonic film culture

concept_purpose: Reframes Nollywood's global circulation as mutual entanglement rather than one-way domination, contesting binary core/periphery oppositions
paper_title: Nollywood internationalism: Filmic entanglements on Nigerian terrain
paper_argument: Argues Nollywood's global diffusion depends on both US streaming corporations and Afro-diasporic informal circulation, generating multiple contested images of Africa, and calls for resisting Nollywood/Hollywood binaries

concept_purpose: A speculative mode that decolonizes the future and imagination to project Black futures and critique present racial subjugation
paper_title: Black Panther, Afrofuturism, and the (Erased) Memory of Patrice Lumumba
paper_argument: Argues that despite Afrofuturism's decolonizing promise, Coogler's Black Panther imaginatively repeats a Cold War plot in which Western power defeats African longing, leading audiences to forget US militarization of Africa and the 1961 murder of Patrice Lumumba

theorist: Saidiya Hartman (afterlife of slavery) / Black Gothic
concept_purpose: Names how the violence of slavery persists in the present (racial mixing, passing, premature death), reworked through Gothic conventions of haunting
paper_title: The Black/Body Gothic: Exhuming and Transcending Racial Mixing, Passing, and Slavery's Afterlives in Lovecraft Country (2020)
paper_argument: Argues that a Black-Lives-Matter-era new wave of Black horror inverts the equation of Blackness with monstrosity, and that Lovecraft Country uses Gothic tropes to exhume and transcend racial passing and slavery's afterlives through Black-centered subjectivity

concept_purpose: Marx's term for collective social knowledge and cooperation incorporated into production, revived to theorize socialized cognitive and embodied labor
paper_title: Articulation, Embodiment, and the General Intellect in Charles Burnett's Killer of Sheep
paper_argument: Reads Charles Burnett's Killer of Sheep through Marx's general intellect, arguing the film renders the articulation and embodiment of socialized Black labor in 1970s Watts as both exploited and a site of collective knowledge

concept_purpose: A non-paranoid, less suspicion-driven mode of critique that seeks to repair rather than only expose damage from prejudice and violence
paper_title: A Reparative Reading of the Atlantic Ocean in Moonlight
paper_argument: Applies Sedgwick's reparative reading to the recurring Atlantic Ocean in Moonlight, arguing the ocean functions as a reparative space of Black queer becoming rather than only a site of Middle Passage trauma

concept_purpose: Names a politicized minor mode of expression by a minority within a major language/cinema that produces another consciousness and collective enunciation
paper_title: The Cinematic Break: DJ Aesthetics and Political Subjectivity in Melvin Van Peebles
paper_argument: Argues Van Peebles's sound/image editing produces a cinematic break (anticipating hip-hop DJ aesthetics) that generates political subjectivity, drawing on Deleuze and Guattari's minor cinema as a means for another consciousness and sensibility

concept_purpose: Names a militant Black, African, anticolonial and feminist filmmaking practice tied to liberation struggle
paper_title: Sambizanga (1972): Aesthetics and politics in the film of Sarah Maldoror—Black, African, anticolonialist, feminist
paper_argument: Frames Maldoror's Sambizanga as an anticolonialist and feminist landmark, reading its aesthetics and politics through the Angolan liberation struggle and the intersection of Blackness, Africanness and gender

theorist: Karl Marx (developed by John Bellamy Foster)
concept_purpose: Names the rupture in the metabolism between humanity and nature produced by capitalist production, depleting the ecological conditions of social reproduction
paper_title: The Aesthetic Rift: An Eco-Marxist Approach to the Capitalist Spatiality of Art
paper_argument: Extends Marx/Foster's metabolic rift into an aesthetic rift, arguing industrial capitalism produced material and imaginary rifts between economics, ecology and aesthetics that fetishize art and the exhibition space under the Capitalocene

concept_purpose: Locates ecological crisis in capitalism's specific organization of power and appropriation of cheap nature, tied to colonial dispossession rather than an undifferentiated humanity
paper_title: Anthropocene as Capitalocene: Soil, Land and Territory in the Artistic Research of Anca Benera and Arnold Estefán
paper_argument: Reads Benera and Estefán's research-based work on devastated landscapes as a Capitalocene critique proposing an alternative epistemology against environmental and political violence rooted in colonial exploitation of cheap nature

concept_purpose: Theorizes Native sovereignty as active sovereign motion and presence that resists the colonial fixity of the vanished Indian
paper_title: Miss Chief and the Art of Decolonial Tease: The Mixedblood Urban Earthdiver and the Flâneur
paper_argument: Reads Kent Monkman's alter ego Miss Chief Eagle Testickle through Vizenor's transmotion, positing the mixedblood urban earthdiver as a decolonial figurehead displacing the modern flâneur

concept_purpose: Describes how Western modernity renders Southern and Indigenous knowledges invisible, proposing intercultural translation across knowledge systems as remedy
paper_title: Miss Chief and the Art of Decolonial Tease: The Mixedblood Urban Earthdiver and the Flâneur
paper_argument: Frames Monkman's parodic art-historical interventions as a post-abyssal ecology of knowledges that uses intercultural translation to displace the canonical authority of Western art history

concept_purpose: Names the unequal condition in which racialized artists are invited into white-dominated institutions on the host's terms, reproducing the exclusion the invitation claims to remedy
paper_title: A Toxic Hospitality?: Racism, Museums and Decolonial Interventions
paper_argument: Argues commissioning artists to decolonise European museums often reproduces Marboeuf's toxic hospitality, generating spatial and temporal inequality that participates in keeping whiteness in place

concept_purpose: Shows how institutional diversity and inclusion documents function as gestures that let institutions appear committed while leaving racialized power intact
paper_title: A Toxic Hospitality?: Racism, Museums and Decolonial Interventions
paper_argument: Maps a continuity between Ahmed's critique of diversity policy and the post-2010 decolonial turn, arguing artistic interventions extend the same logic of appearing to change while preserving whiteness

concept_purpose: Frames land, water and beings as relational animate kin, an ontological alternative to extractive settler-colonial resource economies
paper_title: Mining Matter/s: Bonnie Devine, Anishinaabe Cosmologies, and Uranium Extraction on the Canadian Shield
paper_argument: Uses ecocritical method and Anishinaabe cosmologies to read Bonnie Devine's film Rooster Rock, arguing it investigates uranium extraction's effect on place, beings and ontologies and ties Cold War extraction to community history

concept_purpose: Names value-producing labor yielding informational, affective and communicative content, theorized by autonomists as central to post-Fordist capitalism
paper_title: Living Labor and Social Labor: A Marxian Critique of Immaterial-Labor Theory
paper_argument: Critiques Negri's productivist reading of immaterial labor as independent of capital, arguing its social form is constituted and mediated by capital valorization and encompasses both domination and resistance

concept_purpose: Marx's term for collective social knowledge in production, revived by autonomists to claim socialized cognitive labor exceeds capital's measure
paper_title: Living Labor and Social Labor: A Marxian Critique of Immaterial-Labor Theory
paper_argument: Argues the autonomist reading of general-intellect labor as inherently postcapitalist sets aside the social form of labor and obscures how such labor remains subsumed under capital valorization

concept_purpose: Explains how under capitalism social relations among producers appear as objective value-relations between things, masking the labor that constitutes value
paper_title: Deciphering the Commodity: The Social Code of Value
paper_argument: Argues value is the objective abstract form of capitalist class relations functioning as an automatic social code, and that the commodity's use-value/exchange-value duality is homologous to the sign's signifier/signified duality in Marx's analysis of fetishism

concept_purpose: Explains how the exchange process generates an impersonal autonomized structure of abstract value that precedes and conditions conscious thought
paper_title: Subjects of Exchange: Between Lacan and the Neue Marx-Lektüre
paper_argument: Reads Lacan with the Neue Marx-Lektüre to argue a homology between psychoanalysis and the critique of political economy, showing the autonomization of value (real abstraction) parallels the impersonality of the symbolic order

concept_purpose: Names the proletariat's potential standpoint of the social totality, making the working class the subject-object of history against economistic Marxism
paper_title: Who Are You Calling Vulgar? Lukács, Kautsky, and the Beginnings of Western Marxism
paper_argument: Argues Lukács's project of promoting class consciousness paradoxically depends on the vulgar Marxism it denounces, making vulgar Marxism both precondition and obstacle to revolutionary consciousness

concept_purpose: Rejects the human subject/essence as Marxism's foundation, treating Man as an ideological category in order to ground political intervention
paper_title: Ecology, Politics, and the Crisis of Marxism
paper_argument: Argues posthumanism and renewed Marxist humanism share an ideological structure producing apoliticism before ecological catastrophe, and that an Althusserian theoretical anti-humanism offers a more effective knowledge of political intervention

concept_purpose: Treats culture as a material productive force and names the lived, emergent, pre-formalized experience of a social moment and the institutions producing meaning
paper_title: The Making of Marxism Today: Cultural-Materialist Insights for Democratic Socialist Media Creators
paper_argument: Uses Williams's cultural materialism and structure of feeling under Thatcherism to read the magazine Marxism Today as a counterhegemonic cultural apparatus, drawing lessons for contemporary socialist media against rising fascism

concept_purpose: Names classes excluded from hegemony and the uneven regionalized articulation of class, region and the national-popular
paper_title: The Southern Question and Subaltern Social Groups and Classes
paper_argument: Argues Gramsci's writings on subaltern groups and the Southern Question supply methodological criteria for analyzing race and class in specific conjunctures and can be translated to confront the present conjuncture

concept_purpose: Names exilic, diasporic and postcolonial filmmaking whose multilingual interstitial style accents the dominant cinema and registers displacement
paper_title: West as home in Ruba Nadda's films
paper_argument: Drawing on accented/transnational cinema, reads four films by Syrian-Canadian Ruba Nadda and argues she reconstructs the West as home, building cultural bridges that transcend the exilic poetics of loss and East/West binaries

concept_purpose: Troubles the assumption that a filmmaker sharing a community's identity has unmediated authority to represent it, foregrounding situated partial position
paper_title: Insider/Outsider: Arlene Bowman's Navajo Talking Picture
paper_argument: Uses Trinh's insider/outsider to argue Arlene Bowman's Navajo Talking Picture foregrounds the filmmaker's troubles with translation (she does not speak Navajo) to examine her estranged Diné identity and indict extractivism and the settler-colonial gaze

concept_purpose: Names a figure suspended between presence and absence used to think unsettled non-belonging that resists full materialization
paper_title: Specters of migration: haunting anomalies in Jupiter's Moon (2017), Europe (2022) and The Quiet Migration (2023)
paper_argument: Mobilizes Derrida's spectre to argue recent migration films turn to the spectral and supernatural (the migrant as ghost/anomaly) to convey displacement, alienation and grief, shifting migration fiction away from documentary realism

concept_purpose: Holds that film's vocation is the redemption of physical reality, so location and photographic recording of real places carry historical material meaning
paper_title: Transnational Marseille: film space and layers of history in Transit
paper_argument: Reads Petzold's Transit through Kracauer's realist aesthetics, arguing the film's location shooting collapses past and present and turns Marseille into an instance of messy, actually-existing cosmopolitanism

theorist: Inderpal Grewal & Caren Kaplan (with Ella Shohat)
concept_purpose: Rejects a universalizing global sisterhood, analyzing gender through asymmetrical power, colonial history and cross-border circulation
paper_title: Introduction: Transnational feminist approaches to film and media from the Middle East and North Africa
paper_argument: Brings Grewal & Kaplan's transnational-feminist methodology together with Shohat's feminist film scholarship to argue for reading MENA and diasporic cinema through gender and transnationalism rather than nation-bound or Orientalist frames

concept_purpose: Guards against celebratory uses of transnational, insisting transnational filmmaking be analyzed for how it negotiates the national, the local and power
paper_title: A language not their own: transnational production in 'foreign' dialogue
paper_argument: Framing studies of multilingual/translingual production, argues authorship and authority in transnational filmmaking are reshaped by language barriers and translation, engaging Naficy's accented cinema and critical-transnationalist attention to language as a site of power

concept_purpose: Names other spaces that mirror, contest and invert ordinary social space as real counter-sites
paper_title: Transnational authorship, heterotopia and poetic American West: the practical strategies in Chloé Zhao's Nomadland (2020)
paper_argument: Argues Chloé Zhao constructs a heterotopia of the American West to perform a transnational authorship of mobility and outsiderhood, replacing the real subject with a fictional white protagonist and downplaying the film's politics of race, labor and colonialism
